_comment: Curated CVE -> affected library symbol-name map for the auto-vex-reachability tool (ADR-0006). Dot-prefixed so the .vex/*.json glob skips it; it is NOT an OpenVEX document. Underscore-prefixed keys are metadata the loader ignores. A CVE present here with NONE of its symbols in the binary's dynamic symbol table is auto-marked not_affected (vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path). Absence of a CVE here means 'do not auto-derive', not 'reachable'.
_method: Each list is the set of PUBLIC entry points through which the advisory's vulnerable code is documented to be reachable -- not the internal function named in the advisory text, which never appears in a dynamic symbol table. Internal helpers (parse_tilde, gz_vacate) are listed via their exported callers. Verified 2026-09-07 against the release-attested banlieue-linux-amd64 binary from run 34168810228 (BuildID 8effcf700c9373c65a5f9ee8de0e2af891ee62d7): 154 undefined dynsym entries, none of which is any symbol below. Re-verify with `nm -D --undefined-only bin/banlieue`.
_note_stdio: The banlieue binary imports no C stdio FILE* API at all (no fopen/fdopen/printf/scanf family) -- Rust std goes straight to open/read/write syscalls. That single fact covers the scanf, ungetwc and fopen-mode advisories below.
_note_resolver: The binary DOES import getaddrinfo/freeaddrinfo/gai_strerror/__res_init, so it uses the glibc resolver. The ns_printrr/fp_nquery advisories (CVE-2026-5435, CVE-2026-6238) are in the deprecated DNS record *printing* helpers, which are a separate export surface that the binary does not import.
_note_locale: The binary imports NO locale, iconv, gconv or wide-char conversion symbol whatsoever -- not even setlocale. A process that never calls setlocale stays in the "C" locale for its whole lifetime, so glibc can never select a multibyte JIS charset and never dlopens the SHIFT_JISX0213 / EUC_JISX0213 gconv converters. The Chainguard image reinforces this: its only locale package is glibc-locale-posix. This covers CVE-2026-77117 and CVE-2026-80489.
